correctness.rationale: The exact law has two support points and yields the displayed KL identity directly. Standard Stirling bounds localize global maximizers away from the edges, the exact power series for the central profile gives a unique quartically flat macroscopic maximum at balance, and the 1/N correction forces the O(N^{-1/2}) composition scale. Rescaling gives the limiting quartic profile with unique absolute maximizer |y|=1/2 and value 1/6. No finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The leave-one-out regime is a natural endpoint of finite-population approximation. The result identifies a non-obvious mesoscopic symmetry breaking in the worst KL composition and an explicit second-order gain. It also contrasts structurally with the quarter-population optimizer for maximal density ratio, showing that different approximation criteria select genuinely different worst populations.
